3) Can you provide a quick list of the evidence items procurement will ask for (subprocessor list, data flow map, retention/egress controls) — we prefer a short checklist we can attach to our packet.

Best,

Hi Emma — thanks for the spreadsheet, it's helpful. Short legal summary and proposed deliverables below. I'm keeping this concise so procurement can attach to their packet.

Summary (legal):
- Switzerland is treated as a third country under EU law. For transfers from the EEA to CH, the EU SCCs plus a Swiss addendum are the standard safeguard. There is no single "EU SCCs" document that automatically covers CH/UK; the UK IDTA (or UK Addendum) is separate and required for transfers to/from the UK.
- Practical approach: sign the EU SCCs (module(s) appropriate to your processing), append our Swiss addendum, and also execute the UK IDTA (if you process UK data). We'll provide a mapping so you can see which combination applies by dataset/processing activity.

Deliverables we'll provide by COB Mon (10/25):
- 1-page TIA map: country -> required instrument (EU SCCs / Swiss addendum / UK IDTA)
- Short evidence checklist (subprocessor list, dataflow diagram, SOC2 attestation summary, retention/egress controls, KMS/HSM notes)
- Redlined DPA (if needed) and a clean DPA (redwood-dpa-v3.pdf attached)
- Swiss addendum template + guidance note (we'll flag any vendor-specific caveats)

Notes on timelines & exceptions: we can combine the package into a single PDF for procurement. If Alpen requires notarized attestations for export (some Swiss health orgs request extra proof), flag that now and we'll route to our compliance team — it may add 3–5 business days.

Kim will follow up with the technical artifacts (subprocessor csv + minimal dataflow diagram).

Marissa Cole
Senior Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference
